records.title: Humility, Forgiveness, and Emerging Adult Female Romantic Relationships
records.journal: Journal of marital and family therapy
records.design: cross-sectional survey, serial mediation path analysis
records.population_setting: emerging adult women, N=152, US convenience sample, currently in a romantic relationship
records.key_finding: Perceived humility related to relationship satisfaction via a serial mediation path through self-forgiveness then partner-forgiveness (N=152); effect not reducible to impression management.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports R1 humility as a construct with measured downstream relational benefit (forgiveness -> satisfaction). Directly on the faqr/humility node of T-PHE's sequence, though this is a psychological trait-humility study, not a religious-ethics study; the theological chain (faqr->taqwa->amanah) is an analogy T-PHE draws, not something this paper tests.
records.evidence_level: cross-sectional, single sample, path-analytic mediation (not RCT/longitudinal)

records.title: Intellectual humility is reliably associated with constructive responses to conflict
records.design: two-study correlational/survey design (interpersonal and workplace conflict contexts)
records.population_setting: general adult samples, Study 1 (friends/family conflict) and Study 2 (workplace conflict)
records.key_finding: Intellectual humility (awareness of one's own fallibility) predicted more constructive and less destructive responses to conflict across both interpersonal and workplace conflict contexts, replicated across two studies.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports R1 humility and mechanism 'decision control': humility as awareness of fallibility maps onto T-PHE's faqr (accepting incompleteness) construct and its claimed effect on conflict-handling behaviour is the closest PubMed-indexed analogue to the humility->conscientious-restraint link T-PHE proposes; still an analogy, since T-PHE's sequence is normative/ethical, this evidence is descriptive/associational.
records.evidence_level: correlational, two studies, no intervention

records.title: Intellectual Humility Predicts Empathic Accuracy and Empathic Resilience
records.design: three preregistered studies (two correlational, one experimental manipulation) with mini meta-analysis
records.population_setting: general adult samples, N=533 total across three studies (n=212, n=112, n=209)
records.key_finding: Intellectual humility (IH) positively associated with empathic accuracy (mini meta-analysis across studies), especially toward outgroup members; experimentally manipulated increases in state IH were associated with greater empathic accuracy; IH also predicted empathic resilience (buffering personal distress while maintaining empathic concern).
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports R1 humility -> R3-adjacent openness/perspective-taking mechanism: humility causally (via manipulation) increasing empathic accuracy is evidence that a humility-based safeguard could plausibly support the compassion/openness-to-correction chain T-PHE assumes; complicates any claim of a specific effect size for T-PHE itself, since this is general-population evidence, not evidence for T-PHE's programme.
records.evidence_level: experimental (manipulation study within a three-study design) plus mini meta-analysis; general adult population, not premarital/health-education context

records.title: Intellectual Humility and Responsiveness to Public Health Recommendations
records.design: two correlational survey studies during COVID-19 pandemic
records.population_setting: US adult samples, Study 1 N=541, Study 2 N ranging 265-702
records.key_finding: Higher intellectual humility associated with greater adherence to expert health recommendations (mask-wearing, social distancing) even controlling for political affiliation; association partly mediated by beliefs that mask-wearing is effective and protects others; IH also associated with prosocial traits (agreeableness, benevolence).
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports R1 humility as a construct linked to health-behaviour uptake and openness to correction from external/expert sources, an analogy to T-PHE's claim that humility supports responsiveness to health education content; note this is about deference to public-health expertise, not to a partner or facilitator in an intimate/premarital context, so the analogy is domain-shifted.
records.evidence_level: correlational, cross-sectional, general population, non-relationship context

records.title: A Theory of Cultural Humility
records.design: theory-development paper using Walker and Avant concept/theory-synthesis method
records.population_setting: nursing and health-professions education, theoretical/conceptual (no primary human sample)
records.key_finding: Presents a synthesized theory of cultural humility (antecedents, attributes, outcomes) intended to guide nurses and other professions toward improved cross-cultural interactions and reduced conflict from misunderstood differences in perspective.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports R1/R4: extends cultural humility beyond the foundational Tervalon 1998 formulation with a structured theory of humility's mechanism and outcomes in health-professional practice, relevant to T-PHE's facilitator-side humility/restraint safeguard; it is theoretical, not an outcomes study, so it complicates any claim of measured effect.
records.evidence_level: theoretical/conceptual synthesis, no empirical outcome data

records.title: Rethinking Cultural Competence: Shifting to Cultural Humility
records.design: narrative literature review/position paper
records.population_setting: healthcare and social-services providers, conceptual review
records.key_finding: Review argues cultural competence training has limited demonstrated effectiveness and risks stereotyping/othering patients; proposes cultural humility (self-reflexivity, sharing power with patients, continuous learning) as an alternative orientation to care, going beyond the original Tervalon 1998 formulation into critique of competence-based training outcomes.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports R4 restraint/mechanism decision control: cultural humility framed explicitly as power-sharing and continuous self-correction, an analogy for T-PHE's facilitator conscientious self-restraint (taqwa) in using programme authority/knowledge; complicates T-PHE by showing competence-training evidence base itself is weak, cautioning against assuming humility framing alone guarantees outcomes.
records.evidence_level: narrative review/position paper, not a controlled outcomes study

records.title: S.E.L.F.: Lessons in institutional cultural humility approach from an academic health center
records.design: programme evaluation of an institutional cultural-humility training module (mixed quantitative/qualitative)
records.population_setting: 30,000 employees across a large US health system
records.key_finding: Institution-wide cultural humility training module showed improved attitudes, knowledge and satisfaction post-training; qualitative analysis highlighted perceived utility; authors emphasize a single training is insufficient and ongoing education/dialogue is needed for institutional culture change and accountability.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports R1 humility with an actual outcomes-evaluation beyond Tervalon 1998's conceptual paper, at institutional/health-system scale; also cautions (complicates) T-PHE's implicit assumption that a bounded programme intervention alone can institutionalize humility, since this study explicitly found single-dose training insufficient.
records.evidence_level: pre/post programme evaluation, self-reported attitudes/knowledge/satisfaction, no control group reported in abstract

records.title: Exploring compassion: a meta-analysis of the association between self-compassion and psychopathology
records.design: systematic review and meta-analysis (random-effects), 20 samples from 14 studies, all using the Neff Self-Compassion Scale
records.population_setting: mixed clinical/non-clinical adult samples across included studies
records.key_finding: Large inverse effect size between self-compassion and psychopathology, r=-0.54 (95% CI -0.57 to -0.51, p<.0001); no evidence of significant publication bias; significant heterogeneity across studies.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports the compassion node of T-PHE's sequence (faqr -> humility/compassion) with strong quantitative meta-analytic evidence for compassion's mental-health benefit; this is evidence for self-compassion and mental health generally, not for T-PHE's premarital programme itself — an analogy, not direct support.
records.evidence_level: meta-analysis of correlational studies (Th2-equivalent quantitative synthesis, not causal/RCT evidence)

records.title: The effectiveness of compassion focused therapy with clinical populations: A systematic review and meta-analysis
records.design: systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of RCTs and randomised pilot/feasibility studies, 15 studies (2013-2022)
records.population_setting: clinical populations with mental health difficulties, mixed settings; ~75% female participants
records.key_finding: Compassion Focused Therapy (CFT) improved self-compassion (effect sizes 0.19-0.90), self-criticism (0.15-0.72), self-reassurance (0.43-0.81), and reduced clinical symptomology (e.g. depression 0.24-0.25) versus waitlist control; 7/15 studies rated unclear methodological quality; long-term effects not established.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports compassion as a modifiable, intervention-responsive construct with measured clinical benefit (RCT-level evidence), the strongest causal analogue among the compassion records for T-PHE's claim that compassion-building content could plausibly improve wellbeing; complicates by flagging unclear-quality studies and absence of long-term follow-up, cautioning against overclaiming durability.
records.evidence_level: meta-analysis of RCTs/pilot RCTs (Th1-equivalent for the CFT-outcome link), moderate quality concerns noted by authors

records.title: Self-compassion and relationship maintenance: the moderating roles of conscientiousness and gender
records.journal: Journal of personality and social psychology
records.design: two correlational studies, one experiment, one longitudinal study
records.population_setting: romantic couples/intimates, mixed community samples (US)
records.key_finding: Among men high in conscientiousness, self-compassion was associated with greater motivation to correct interpersonal mistakes, more constructive problem-solving, more accommodation, and fewer declines in marital satisfaction; among men low in conscientiousness, associations reversed; among women, self-compassion was positively associated with corrective motivation and satisfaction change regardless of conscientiousness.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Complicates a simple 'more compassion is always better' reading of T-PHE's safeguard: shows self-compassion's relational benefit is conditional on conscientiousness (a self-regulation trait), suggesting T-PHE's safeguard sequence (compassion feeding into restraint) may need conscientiousness/self-regulation as a moderating condition, not an automatic consequence, especially for men in this sample.
records.evidence_level: mixed correlational, experimental and longitudinal design (multi-study), general (non-premarital, non-Muslim, non-Thai) samples

records.title: The predictive effect of self-compassion on relationship satisfaction and conflict resolution styles in romantic relationships in nursing students
records.design: cross-sectional survey, linear regression
records.population_setting: 356 nursing students (68.5% female); country not stated in the abstract text itself (journal is Turkish-based and author name suggests Turkey, but this is an inference, not an abstract-confirmed fact)
records.key_finding: Self-compassion significantly predicted relationship satisfaction and conflict-resolution styles (positive conflict resolution, negative conflict resolution, retreat) in romantic relationships (p<.05).
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports the compassion -> conflict-handling link relevant to T-PHE's mechanism decision control, in a young-adult, premarital-adjacent (unmarried students) sample closer in life-stage to T-PHE's target population than most other records; still not a Thai or Muslim sample, and cross-sectional so directionality is not established.
records.evidence_level: cross-sectional correlational (regression), single country/sample

records.title: Relationship satisfaction in Black heterosexual couples: The role of self-compassion and openness
records.journal: Journal of marital and family therapy
records.design: cross-sectional dyadic survey, common-fate moderated mediation model
records.population_setting: 210 Black married heterosexual couples, US
records.key_finding: Higher self-compassion in both spouses associated with lower negative interaction in the relationship; couples' negative interaction suppressed the positive effect of self-compassion on relationship satisfaction; for wives, open communication moderated how self-compassion related to satisfaction, and this pathway depended on perceived racial discrimination.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Complicates a straightforward compassion-to-satisfaction claim: shows the compassion -> satisfaction pathway can be suppressed by negative interaction and is contingent on open communication and external stressors (discrimination) — evidence that T-PHE's safeguard sequence likely needs supporting conditions (open communication, low conflict) to translate compassion into relational benefit, not a direct or guaranteed chain.
records.evidence_level: cross-sectional dyadic survey with moderated-mediation modeling, married (not premarital) US Black couples

records.title: Empathy Mediates the Relations between Working Memory and Perpetration of Intimate Partner Violence and Aggression
records.design: laboratory-based observational study with conflict-discussion coding and self/partner-report
records.population_setting: 49 men in heterosexual relationships, community sample
records.key_finding: Working memory positively related to cognitive and affective empathy and negatively related to men's physical abuse perpetration and observed aggression; effects of working memory on aggression and IPV frequency were fully mediated by empathy (cognitive/affective respectively).
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports the theoretical rationale for R4/mechanism decision control: empathy (a compassion-adjacent construct) mediating the link between cognitive-executive deficits and IPV perpetration supports the plausibility that fostering empathy/compassion could reduce coercive or aggressive relational behaviour, an analogy for why T-PHE positions compassion as protective; small sample (N=49), so effect sizes should not be generalized.
records.evidence_level: observational/mediation analysis, small sample, single study (not meta-analytic)

records.title: Childhood Sexual Abuse, Dyadic Empathy, and Intimate Partner Violence Among Men Seeking Psychological Help
records.design: cross-sectional survey with mediation/moderation analysis
records.population_setting: 198 men aged 18-69 seeking help for relationship problems (clinical/help-seeking sample)
records.key_finding: Emotional empathy mediated and moderated the link between childhood sexual abuse (CSA) and perpetrated psychological (not physical) IPV; cognitive empathy negatively associated with both physical and psychological IPV, while emotional empathy was positively associated with psychological IPV, showing a complex, construct-specific pattern.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Complicates a simple 'empathy reduces IPV' narrative that would support T-PHE's compassion safeguard: shows emotional empathy can be positively associated with psychological IPV perpetration in a help-seeking clinical sample, while cognitive empathy is protective — evidence that compassion/empathy constructs are not uniformly protective and must be specified (cognitive vs emotional) when used to ground a safeguard.
records.evidence_level: cross-sectional, clinical help-seeking sample, single study

records.title: ADHD in Childhood and/or Adulthood as a Risk Factor for Domestic Violence or Intimate Partner Violence: A Systematic Review
records.design: systematic review of case-control and cohort studies
records.population_setting: adults with childhood and/or adult ADHD, general/clinical samples across included studies
records.key_finding: Cohort studies identified hyperactive, impulsive and inattention symptoms (markers of poor self-regulation/self-control) as risk factors for adult IPV perpetration; comorbid Conduct Disorder and Antisocial Personality Disorder acted as mediators in three studies; existing DV/IPV treatment programmes shown to have minimal impact to date.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports the self-regulation/self-control node (angle d) as evidence-based: poor self-regulation (via ADHD symptomatology) is a documented risk factor for IPV perpetration, providing indirect support for T-PHE's premise that strengthening self-regulation/conscientious restraint (taqwa-analogue) could plausibly reduce coercive-relational risk; complicates by noting current DV/IPV treatment programmes (not specifically premarital education) have shown limited effectiveness, a caution against assuming any programme design solves this.
records.evidence_level: systematic review of case-control/cohort studies (Th2-equivalent, observational only, not RCT)

records.title: A Systematic Review of the Psychosocial Mechanism Underlying the Pathway from Intra-Familial Victimization in Childhood to Intimate Relationship Violence in Adolescence and Adulthood
records.design: mixed-methods systematic review, 17 peer-reviewed studies
records.population_setting: individuals with a history of intra-familial childhood victimization (IF-CV), mixed adolescent/adult samples across included studies
records.key_finding: Attachment style moderates and Early Maladaptive Schema mediates the link between intra-familial childhood victimization and later relationship violence; Sense-of-Self components — self-control, self-blame, self-worth, self-esteem — emerged as strong contributors to the mechanism; identity-resolution as a potential mediator has not yet been studied.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports self-regulation (self-control as part of 'Sense-of-Self') as a mechanistic contributor within the pathway from childhood victimization to relationship-violence risk, indirect support for angle (d); this is a mechanism review, not intervention evidence, so it does not show that building self-control via a programme like T-PHE changes downstream violence risk.
records.evidence_level: mixed-methods systematic review of mechanism/mediation studies, observational, no intervention data

records.title: Psychometric Validation of Trust, Commitment, and Satisfaction Scales to Measure Marital Relationship Quality Among Newly Married Women in Nepal
records.journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
records.design: two-wave psychometric validation study (exploratory + confirmatory factor analysis), 96% 6-month retention
records.population_setting: 200 newly married women aged 18-25, rural Nawalparasi district, Nepal (South Asian, comparable regional context)
records.key_finding: Validated single-factor trust and commitment scales and a two-factor satisfaction scale for South Asian newly married women; good internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha 0.79-0.96) and significant criterion validity with relationship happiness (r=0.63-0.72, p<.001); test-retest reliability moderate-to-low (r=0.21-0.51), attributed to genuine early-marriage relationship change.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports angle (e) trustworthiness/responsibility constructs: provides a validated, region-relevant (South Asian, low/middle-income, newly married) measurement tool for trust and commitment that a T-PHE evaluation could plausibly adapt for a Thai premarital population; a measurement-development study, not an outcomes or intervention study, so it does not itself show T-PHE would work.
records.evidence_level: psychometric validation study, observational, newly married (not premarital) South Asian sample

records.title: Even Though the Long Distance: Are We Still Going on? Dyadic Trust, Relationship Maintenance Behaviors, and Relationship Quality Among Emerging Adulthoods
records.design: cross-sectional survey with serial mediation modeling
records.population_setting: emerging adults in long-distance romantic relationships of at least 6 months
records.key_finding: Relationship maintenance behaviors predicted relationship quality both directly and indirectly through dyadic trust; openness and positivity were particularly important in building trust, which in turn increased overall relationship quality.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports angle (e): trust functions as a mediating mechanism between relational behaviour (openness, positivity — humility-adjacent constructs) and relationship quality, an analogy for how T-PHE's humility/openness safeguard could theoretically translate into trust and relationship quality; sample is emerging-adult, non-Thai, non-premarital-specific (long-distance daters).
records.evidence_level: cross-sectional, single-study serial mediation, general population sample

records.title: The role of religiosity and spirituality in interpersonal violence: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.journal: Revista brasileira de psiquiatria (Sao Paulo, Brazil)
records.design: systematic review (67 studies) and meta-analysis (43 studies) of observational studies, across seven databases
records.population_setting: mixed general-population and clinical samples across included studies (16,599 records screened); subanalysis notes stronger association among adolescents
records.key_finding: Higher religiosity/spirituality significantly associated with decreased physical and sexual aggression, but not with domestic violence specifically; association more prevalent among adolescents; studies rated as sufficient methodological quality overall (26.8% cohort design).
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports and complicates angle (f) simultaneously: religiosity/spirituality shows a protective association with physical/sexual aggression generally (partial support for T-PHE grounding a safeguard in religiously-inflected constructs like taqwa/amanah), but explicitly did NOT find protection for domestic violence specifically — directly complicates any claim that religiosity-linked constructs reduce IPV/domestic violence in intimate partnerships, the outcome most relevant to T-PHE's premarital safeguard.
records.evidence_level: systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies (Th2-equivalent), not RCT, general (non-Muslim-specific, non-Thai) samples

records.title: The Power of Women's Faith in Coping with Intimate Partner Violence: Systematic Literature Review
records.design: systematic literature review, 18 studies
records.population_setting: women IPV victims/survivors in Christian families (denomination not further specified in abstract)
records.key_finding: Reviewed 18 studies on IPV in Christian families; IPV prevalence in Christian families not higher or lower than general population; religious values/practice, combined with other factors, can provide protection and support both in preventing violence and in recovery, though religiosity combined with other factors may also contribute to victim vulnerability or perpetrator's power in some cases.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Complicates angle (f)/(g): shows religiosity's relationship to IPV is bidirectional (protective in some pathways, risk-amplifying in others depending on context), directly relevant caution for T-PHE's ethical safeguard grounded in religious constructs (faqr/taqwa/amanah) — religious framing is not a guaranteed protective factor and must be evaluated for how it is operationalized, not assumed protective by label; note this evidence is on Christian, not Muslim, samples, so it is an analogy across religious traditions, not direct evidence for T-PHE's Islamic-ethics-grounded sequence.
records.evidence_level: systematic literature review (qualitative synthesis), observational studies only

records.title: Socio-Cognitive Integration Theory (SCIT): A contextual model for mental health in Islamic-Asian societies: Integrative review
records.design: integrative literature review (conceptual model synthesis)
records.population_setting: conceptual/theoretical, drawing on literature from six Islamic-Asian countries (Iran, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, UAE, Afghanistan, Pakistan)
records.key_finding: Proposes Socio-Cognitive Integration Theory: mental health conceptualized as alignment between personal cognitive appraisals and culturally sanctioned social roles; religious narratives, familial obligations and social expectations found (via synthesis) to shape psychological resilience and emotional stability in Muslim-majority societies.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports angle (f)/mechanism decision control as a theoretical (not outcome) analogue: offers a culturally-grounded psychological framework for how religiously-inflected role-obligation constructs (analogous to amanah/entrusted responsibility) relate to mental-health functioning in Muslim-majority contexts, useful as conceptual scaffolding; it is a theory-synthesis paper with no primary empirical/outcome data of its own, so it cannot support any effectiveness claim for T-PHE.
records.evidence_level: conceptual/theoretical integrative review, no primary quantitative outcome data

records.title: Obtaining religious and spiritual competencies for relationship therapy: Outcomes of Competency Addressing Religion and Spirituality (CARS) training
records.design: training-outcomes study with switching-replication design (immediate vs delayed treatment), three measurement waves plus qualitative interviews (n=10 subsample)
records.population_setting: 174 graduate students and mental-health professionals
records.key_finding: 5-hour online religious/spiritual (R/S) competency training, built on principles of cultural humility, nonanxious presence and differentiation, produced significant improvements in self-efficacy, attitude, frequency of R/S-integrated practice, and global relational R/S competency, sustained in the immediate-treatment group at follow-up.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports angles (b)/(g): demonstrates a humility-grounded, values/spirituality-explicit training curriculum for relationship-facing professionals producing measured competency gains with a controlled (switching-replication) design — the closest PubMed-indexed analogue among all records to a 'humility-based, values-based relational intervention with measured outcomes'; still trains clinicians, not couples, and is not premarital-specific or Thai/Muslim-specific, so remains an analogy for T-PHE's own (untested) couple-facing programme.
records.evidence_level: controlled training-outcomes study (switching-replication, quasi-experimental), self-report outcome measures, professional (not client/couple) sample

records.title: Cultural adaptation and pilot evaluation of the Couple Learning Program (CLP) among young Turkish couples: A mixed-method study
records.design: pilot randomized controlled trial, mixed-methods, pre/post/follow-up
records.population_setting: 8 couples (premarital, culturally-adapted programme), Turkey, plus a 2-couple feasibility phase
records.key_finding: Six-session culturally-adapted Couple Learning Program significantly improved conflict-resolution strategies (exit, voice, neglect dimensions; not loyalty) and produced a significant increase in relationship satisfaction at follow-up only (not immediately post-intervention); qualitative data showed improved empathetic communication and structured problem-solving; no attrition.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Directly supports angle (g) as the strongest structural analogue found: a culturally-adapted, values/skills-based premarital couple intervention with a pilot RCT design and measured relational outcomes, closely paralleling what T-PHE proposes to build and test; complicates by showing satisfaction gains emerged only at follow-up (not immediately), and by its very small sample (8 couples) — a pilot feasibility signal, not evidence of established effectiveness, and this must not be read as validating T-PHE, which remains untested.
records.evidence_level: pilot RCT, very small sample (N=8 couples), feasibility/preliminary-effectiveness evidence only

records.title: Knowledge improvement on premarital HIV counseling with PAUSE flipchart versus conventional method: a cluster randomised controlled trial
records.design: parallel cluster-randomised controlled trial, 8 public primary healthcare clinics
records.population_setting: Malay-literate adult clients undergoing mandatory premarital HIV testing/counselling, Johor Bahru, Malaysia (Muslim-majority setting)
records.key_finding: Both intervention (PAUSE flipchart) and control (routine verbal counselling) groups showed significant HIV-knowledge increases post-counselling (p<.001); intervention group's mean score increase (6.99, 95% CI 6.01-7.97) was significantly higher than control's (3.99, 95% CI 2.89-5.09); flipchart rated highly understandable (PEMAT-P mean 95.92).
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports angle (g)/consent-adjacent evidence base: a Muslim-majority-country, mandatory premarital-counselling, cluster-RCT with a validated knowledge outcome — directly comparable design and population context to what T-PHE's own effectiveness evaluation would need to resemble, though it targets HIV knowledge rather than the humility/consent/restraint constructs T-PHE grounds itself in, so it supports feasibility of rigorous premarital-counselling RCTs in a comparable setting rather than T-PHE's specific content.
records.evidence_level: cluster RCT (Th1-equivalent for the specific outcome measured), knowledge outcome only, no behavioural/relational outcome

records.title: Characteristics and Effectiveness of Premarital Thalassaemia Educational Interventions Worldwide: A scoping review
records.design: scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, 8 included studies
records.population_setting: adolescents and young adults, culturally diverse and resource-limited settings globally
records.key_finding: Premarital thalassaemia educational interventions (traditional, technology-based, or culturally adapted) consistently improved knowledge (p<.001) across studies, but behavioural outcomes such as screening uptake were inconsistent; socio-cultural barriers limited translation of knowledge gains into behaviour change.
records.relevance_to_tphe: Supports angle (g) as base-rate evidence for the premarital-education field generally: shows a consistent, cross-context pattern that premarital education interventions reliably raise knowledge but do NOT reliably change behaviour — a direct and important caution against assuming T-PHE's knowledge/humility content will translate into behavioural or relational outcomes; complicates T-PHE by flagging the knowledge-behaviour gap as the field's dominant limitation, not a hypothetical risk.
records.evidence_level: scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) of mixed-design primary studies, not itself a meta-analysis of effect sizes

gaps_noted: No PubMed-indexed record was found testing the specific humility -> compassion -> conscientious self-restraint -> entrusted-responsibility (amanah) sequence itself, in any tradition; this ethical chain is not an object of empirical psychological study in the indexed literature, so all support above is by analogy to component constructs, never to the full T-PHE sequence.

No PubMed-indexed intimate partner violence perpetration meta-analysis specifically for self-control/self-regulation/conscientiousness was found (search e/d query q6 returned only one weak match, 30887404, excluded as off-topic); available evidence (25995243 ADHD; 40035136 mechanism review) is indirect/observational, not the target meta-analytic evidence class the brief asked for.

No PubMed-indexed record on trustworthiness/accountability constructs specific to health-care ethics (angle e, health-care-ethics half) was retrieved; searches (e2/accountability+health-care-ethics) returned unrelated genetics/pharmacy-education records, suggesting this specific pairing is thin in the indexed literature or requires different terminology.

No Muslim-sample or Thailand-based record was found for the intellectual-humility or self-compassion literatures (angles a/c); the religiosity-IPV evidence located (36331229, 33704630) is Brazilian-mixed-sample and Christian-family literature respectively, not Muslim samples, despite the query explicitly requesting Muslim samples where indexed — none were indexed for this specific construct pairing.

Cultural humility 'outcomes evidence beyond Tervalon 1998' is present (42656867, 40705620) but is process/attitude/knowledge outcome evidence (training satisfaction, self-efficacy, competency scores), not patient-health-outcome evidence in the strict sense (e.g., mortality, clinical biomarkers, care-utilization); true clinical-outcomes evidence for cultural humility specifically (isolated from cultural competence) remains sparse in this search.
limits_of_this_search: This search covers PubMed/MEDLINE only via NCBI E-utilities esearch/efetch (no WebSearch/WebFetch used); 17 queries run, 26 abstracts read via efetch abstract XML. Selection was investigator (AI-agent) judgment from among the top-ranked hits of each query, not a systematic/PRISMA-compliant screening of all retrieved records, and no forward/backward citation chaining or grey-literature search was performed. All records are offered as psychological/health-services analogies to the components of T-PHE's faqr->humility/compassion->taqwa->amanah ethical sequence; none constitute evidence that T-PHE itself is effective, and several records (37752743, 35089108, 33704630, 36331229, 40979613) explicitly complicate a simple protective reading of humility/compassion/religiosity constructs. This document is for the medical-science-register public repository only and deliberately excludes theological literature per task instructions.
